text:
matt: Heads up — saw a 3-4x tail latency regression on small decode requests (~8 tokens) after the kernel-routing change last night. Investigating.

anya: ugh. is this prefill or decode path?

matt: decode path. prefill numbers look stable. Only seeing the spike when continuous-batching is on and routing picks the fused/paged Flash variant for small batches.

devin: do we have KV cache metrics around fragmentation or page churn? could be cache miss storms.

matt: good call. I pulled KV cache evict counters and saw a small burst correlated with the spike window.

kevin: micro-benched the kernels on a local titan yesterday. For batch=1..8: fused-flash (default) 1-token throughput ok, but at 6-8 tokens latency jumps vs smallbatch-optimized kernel. numbers: 
- fused-flash batch=4 mean=12ms p95=30ms
- small-opt batch=4 mean=9ms p95=12ms
- fused-flash batch=8 mean=28ms p95=85ms

anya: interesting — sounds like kernel selection mispredicts when sequence len and kvpage layout combine to trigger a slow path. any logs from kernel selector?

matt: selector logs show rule: prefer fused-flash when seq_len<=64 && batch_size<=16 && model.arch=decoder. That was intended to consolidate, but apparently fused-flash has poor memory behavior for small decode windows.

devin: could be GPU TLB / page fault behavior for paged attention. If KV pages are fragmented, the fused kernel's memory access pattern may thrash. did you try forcing paged vs non-paged?

anya: I ran perf counters on a repro pod. Dump: 
```
GPU DRAM Reads: 1.2e9
PageFaults (device): 42
L2 Misses: 3.1e7
SM Util: spiky 10-80%
```
Page faults line up with tail latency spikes.

sara: can we short-circuit routing to pick the small-batch decode kernel for <12 tokens as a canary? That should reduce tails while we debug.

matt: yes I can push a policy override to the canary pool. Want to do that after the next deploy window.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: redwood/infra@a7d2c3 -> canary-runtime, CI perf tests running.

perf-bot: CI microbench summary: after a7d2c3: small-decode p95 increased from 14ms -> 54ms on fused-flash variant (repro for baseline). Full log: http://ci/internal/bench/1803456789

kevin: posted a short benchmark harness in /tmp that toggles kernel selection per request. quick numbers look like: fused-flash has worse p95 for batches 5..12, small-opt consistent.

devin: hypothesis: fused/paged Flash variant uses a tiled gather that assumes contiguous KV pages; when KV cache is fragmented (due to continuous batching interleaving different seq lens) it issues more device page faults. small-opt keeps accesses more linear.

anya: can we add a cheap metric to kernel selector: if kv_fragmentation_score>THRESH then avoid fused-flash for decode? compute score per-gpu from evict counters + page faults.

matt: I can log a candidate metric today. Will add a 0/1 feature so we can backfill and test.

kevin: Also worth running the fused-flash under RTX memcheck to see if there's a pathological path.

devin: for immediate mitigation: 1) override routing to small-opt for decode <12 tokens, 2) increase KV page coalescing window (reduce fragmentation), 3) add metric to selector.

matt: I'll do 1 and 3. sara can you take 2?

sara: on it. I'll try bumping coalesce_window from 50ms -> 200ms on canary.

anya: after we stabilize, we should add an e2e test that simulates continuous-batching with mixed seq_lens to catch regressions.

matt: agreed. action items: matt=override routing canary + add kv_fragmentation metric; sara=coalesce window change; kevin=run detailed memtrace; devin=write regression test harness. I'll post follow-up in this thread when canary lands. :thumbsup:

kevin: one more note — fused-flash still wins on steady-state big batches. this is a routing nuance, not a kernel removal.

matt: exactly. goal is smarter routing, not removing fused-flash.

deploy-bot: canary deployed to 3 hosts (ids: i-0a1,i-0b2,i-0c3), routing override active.

matt: initial canary metrics look promising — p95 down from ~60ms -> ~14ms on canary hosts. will monitor for 2 hours then roll to more.

anya: nice. keep an eye on throughput; coalescing might increase memory pressure.

matt: noted. thanks all.
